title: Arithmetic stable genus locus is open and bounded
statement: Let $g\geq2$ and let $\mathfrak C_{\mathbf Z}$ be the fibred groupoid of proper flat finitely presented curve families of algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with cartesian arrows [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli]. Its full subcategory of families all of whose geometric fibres are connected stable curves of arithmetic genus $g$ is an open algebraic substack, in the sense of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], contained in the nonempty nodal locus [def-sfb-curve-moduli-groupoids]. More explicitly, for each $X\to T$ in $\mathfrak C_{\mathbf Z}$ there is an open $T_g^{\mathrm{st}}\subseteq T$, compatible with every base change, such that $T'\to T$ factors through it exactly when $X_{T'}\to T'$ is a stable unpointed genus-$g$ family in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Over this open the algebraic space $X$ is a scheme and the family admits a closed embedding into the projective bundle of a finite-rank locally free module, as required by that definition. The resulting open substack is equivalent, over the category of schemes, to $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$ in that definition. Its field-valued point space is quasi-compact: every covering by open subsets has a finite subcover, for the topology characterized by inverse images under smooth surjective scheme atlases. A field-valued point is an object over a field, with two such objects identified when they become isomorphic over a common field extension. An open substack is a full subcategory whose scheme pullbacks are open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. No field-base or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $T$, and the assertions include disconnected and nonreduced test schemes.

source.place: Tags 0E76 (lemma-stable-curves), 0E78 (lemma-stable-one-piece-per-genus), 0E9B (lemma-stable-quasi-compact). Stable-family scheme/projective-bundle comparison: relative dualizing sheaf discussion and the stable-family discussion before 0E76; tricanonical boundedness in proof of 0E9B.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. By [lem-sfb-arithmetic-nodal-curve-stack-smooth], $\mathfrak C_S$ is algebraic and its nonempty nodal subcategory is open. For a family $f:X\to T$, denote its nodal open by $N\subseteq T$. Apply [lem-sfb-curve-h0-genus-strata] to $X_N\to N$ and take its rank-$g$ open-and-closed locus inside the scalar-$H^0$ open; call the resulting open of $T$ $B$. Nodal fibres are geometrically reduced, so the last clause of that node identifies $B$ exactly with the locus of geometrically connected nonempty nodal fibres of arithmetic genus $g$. Both constructions commute with every base change. In particular all fibres over $B$ are schemes.

On $X_B/B$, [lem-sfb-nodal-relative-dualizing-line] supplies the line $\omega$ and identifies its geometric restrictions with the fibre dualizing lines. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-ample-locus] to $\omega$, and call its open $A\subseteq B$. It is characterized by ampleness on the geometric fibres, commutes with arbitrary base change, and $X_A$ is a scheme. By [lem-sfb-nodal-canonical-positivity-tricanonical], for each geometric fibre (connected, reduced, proper, nodal and genus $g\geq2$), ampleness of its dualizing line is equivalent to the required component stability inequalities: a genus-zero component has at least three branches at nodes, and a genus-one component has at least one. Thus $A$ is precisely the stable fibre locus, already with schematic total space.

Take $L=\omega_{X_A/A}^{\otimes3}$. The tricanonical clause of [lem-sfb-nodal-canonical-positivity-tricanonical] says on every geometric fibre that $L$ is very ample and $H^1(L)=0$. The morphism $X_A\to A$ is still proper, flat and finitely presented, and has one-dimensional fibres. Therefore [lem-sfb-fibrewise-very-ample-evaluation] applies: $E=f_*L$ is finite locally free and its evaluation gives a closed immersion $X_A\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_A(E)$, commuting with arbitrary base change. This proves the global projective-bundle assertion even when $A$ is nonreduced, disconnected or not quasi-compact; it does not appeal to the insufficient general assertion that a relatively ample proper family over an arbitrary base is projective.

source.place: Tags 0E76 (lemma-stable-curves), 0E8X (curves.tex, lemma-tricanonical); spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0CTM and spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 05XA for relative evaluation

proof.text: Set $T_g^{\mathrm{st}}=A$. The preceding three steps show that factoring through $A$ implies every clause of an unpointed stable genus-$g$ family in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. Conversely, such a family is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper], and its fibre conditions and [lem-sfb-nodal-canonical-positivity-tricanonical] force its base map to factor first through $N$, then $B$, then $A$, by their defining properties. The same reasoning applies to every $T'\to T$, including the empty base. Uniqueness of factorization through an open identifies the scheme test of the full subcategory with $A$ [def-sfb-open-moduli-substack]. Its objects are schemes by step 2; between such objects the cartesian algebraic-space arrows are exactly the cartesian scheme arrows. The identification therefore gives the claimed equivalence with $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$ over schemes, respecting pullbacks and retaining all automorphisms.

source.place: Tags 0E76 (lemma-stable-curves), 0E78 (lemma-stable-one-piece-per-genus), and section-open: scheme-test universal property

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak M$ denote this full open subcategory of $\mathfrak C_S$. The ambient category is algebraic by [lem-sfb-arithmetic-nodal-curve-stack-smooth]. Its every scheme test of $\mathfrak M$ is the open just constructed, so [lem-sfb-open-stack-algebraic-lfp] proves that $\mathfrak M$ is algebraic. Its containment in the nonempty nodal substack follows from $A\subseteq N$. This establishes algebraicity without using quasi-compactness or an atlas of the stable moduli groupoid as an input.

For boundedness put $n=5g-6\geq4$ and $P(t)=(6g-6)t+1-g$. For every field-valued stable object $C/K$, [lem-sfb-stable-curve-pluricanonical-linear-series] with exponent $3$ gives a tricanonical closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_K$, since $h^0(\omega_C^3)=5g-5$, with Hilbert polynomial $P$. Use [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] for $\mathbf P^n_S$ itself (identity closed immersion), and denote its fixed-$P$ representing scheme by $H$. Its universal closed subscheme $Z\subset\mathbf P^n_H$ is flat and finitely presented over $H$, is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper], and all its geometric fibres have polynomial $P$. Since $P$ is nonzero they are nonempty; by [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-dimension] their dimension is one. Thus $Z/H$ is an object of $\mathfrak C_S$, to which steps 1--4 apply. Write $V\subseteq H$ for its stable genus-$g$ open.

source.place: Tag 0E9B (lemma-stable-quasi-compact), expanding moduli.tex Tag 0E96 (lemma-bounded-polarized) through the Hilbert scheme and using the complete-system projective dimension

proof.text: The Hilbert node gives $H$ of finite type over $S$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives that $H$ is Noetherian, explicitly including the fact that $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian. Its open subscheme $V$ is Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The universal family restricted to $V$ defines a morphism $V\to\mathfrak M$. It is surjective on field-valued point classes: given $C/K$, choose a basis of $H^0(C,\omega_C^3)$; its embedding from step 6 gives a $K$-point of $H$ classifying exactly $C$ with that embedding, and this point factors through $V$ because $C$ is stable. Forgetting the embedding returns the original point of $\mathfrak M$. No universal choice of bases, and no smoothness or surjectivity of $V\to\mathfrak M$ as a representable morphism, is required.

source.place: Tag 0E9B (lemma-stable-quasi-compact), Hilbert argument of moduli.tex Tag 0E96; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, properties.tex Tags 01OW and 01OZ

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], the point map $|V|\to|\mathfrak M|$ is continuous for exactly the smooth-atlas topology in the statement. For an open cover $\{O_i\}$ of $|\mathfrak M|$, its inverse images cover $|V|$, hence finitely many cover $|V|$ by step 7. The point-surjectivity just proved implies that the same finite collection of $O_i$ covers $|\mathfrak M|$. This is the asserted quasi-compactness.
